summary:
Project Overview The SPHEREx Sky Motion Viewer is a web app that automatically detects and analyzes moving solar system objects using real observations from the NASA SPHEREx mission. It deals with the problem of finding possible moving objects in large astronomical data sets while guaranteeing that the results are reliable, transparent and reusable.

The application retrieves SPHEREx observations, applies image alignment, differencing, and automated motion detection to identify candidates and reconstruct their trajectories. Detected objects are cross-checked against Gaia DR3, AllWISE, and IMCCE SkyBoT catalogs to distinguish known sources from candidates requiring further investigation.

Testability and scientific reproducibility are central to our solution. The prototype successfully passed 179/180 synthetic detection checks and supports automated validation across its processing pipeline. Its Download Full Data Package feature exports structured observations, trajectories, catalog matches, and processing metadata in interoperable formats for independent verification and further scientific analysis.

By transforming complex NASA observations into actionable, verifiable results, our project makes astronomical motion detection more accessible and supports future research and potential discoveries.

==================================

Project Overview

SPHEREx Sky Motion Viewer is a web-based tool that detects and analyses moving bodies from actual astronomical data from NASA’s SPHEREx project. We solve the problem of how to effectively identify potential targets containing moving bodies, whilst allowing others to verify our results. We process real data from SPHEREx, to create potential candidates, giving estimated paths, additional data, initial classifications and complete packages to allow further scientific analysis.

Moving Object Detection

The user selects a region of the sky and a period of time for observations. The tool will then retrieve relevant SPHEREx observations from NASA’s Infrared Science Archive (IRSA). It will stack these images, perform subtraction, remove noise and identify moving bodies. The detections are then linked together to form a path estimation. The speed and direction of an object can be estimated with this. Additionally, potential asteroids can be identified. The candidates will then be compared to catalogues such as Gaia DR3, AllWISE and IMCCE SkyBoT. They will then be classified as Known, Unmatched or Inconclusive. Additional information and data will be given. Unmatched candidates will be prioritised for verification.

Testing

Our project includes a testing component that allows us to automatically test our moving body detection, image processing, APIs, catalogues and data. The prototype had a success rate of 179/180 across 20 randomly generated synthetic scenarios. There were no false candidates. The API tests had a success rate of 41/41, detection and classifications had a success rate of 20/20 and the Data Contract had a success rate of 35/35. Finally, we successfully retrieved 247 real frames of Barnard’s Star from SPHEREx. This shows that our project has been well engineered and could use more scientific verification.

Download Full Data Package

With our Download Full Data Package tool we are able to create a complete, versioned, machine-readable ZIP file with detections, single observations, path estimations, catalogue matches, processing information, origin of sources and checksums. It supports CSV, JSON, VOTable and ECSV. This can then be used for verification, analysis and processing using external astronomical tools and future JPL/MPC integration. Any missing data and requirements for verification will be noted.

Impact

SPHEREx Sky Motion Viewer is intended to make detecting motion in astronomical data easier, clear and reproducible. With our tool we are able to give users, students and citizen scientists the ability to identify candidates, with testing, to analyse real data from NASA.
